Cellular calls were easy: the laptop is the phone's Bluetooth hands-free headset, and a headset is told about incoming calls. WeChat calls were not. Apple's ANCS , the Apple Notification Center Service, sends every notification on the phone to a paired Bluetooth LE accessory: which app, the title, the text, and the buttons on it. Verification means checking the signature with an algorithm you chose, not the one the token names , then checking the claims: exp (with a small clock skew allowance), iss , and above all aud , so a token issued for one service can't be replayed against another. articles.title: TI-84 ERR:WINDOW RANGE? It's a 10-Second Fix — Press ZOOM, Then 6
articles.excerpt: Your window settings contradict themselves — usually Xmin is bigger than Xmax. One reset puts them right. Your TI-84 just stopped you with ERR:WINDOW RANGE, right in the middle of graphing. The functi…
articles.body: Your window settings contradict themselves — usually Xmin is bigger than Xmax. One reset puts them right. Your TI-84 just stopped you with ERR:WINDOW RANGE, right in the middle of graphing. The function is fine. The numbers are fine. The problem is the window itself — the settings that tell the calculator which part of the graph to draw contradict each other, so it can't draw anything at all. The good news: this is one of the easiest TI-84 errors to fix. It takes about 10 seconds, and you don't even need to diagnose it first. What ERR:WINDOW RANGE means The graph window is defined by Xmin, Xmax, Ymin, Ymax (and Xscl, Yscl, the tick-mark spacing). The rule is simple: Xmin must be less than Xmax, and Ymin must be less than Ymax.

articles.title: Node.js Private Image Buffers — 4 Storage Choices for Auditable Uploads
articles.excerpt: For a healthtech receipt pipeline, keep the generated image private, upload its Buffer from the backend, and save only the object key plus metadata in your database. That is the cleanest way to preser…
articles.body: For a healthtech receipt pipeline, keep the generated image private, upload its Buffer from the backend, and save only the object key plus metadata in your database. That is the cleanest way to preserve an audit trail without handing storage credentials to a browser. The deciding constraint is access control versus delivery simplicity: a private object needs an authorization check and a temporary download URL, while a public URL is easy to deliver but hard to retract. Short answer: generate the image on the server, write it to a private S3-compatible bucket under a unique key such as generations/{userId}/{date}/{jobId}.png , then issue a presigned GET only after the requesting user is authorized. Keep the receipt row as the source of business truth.

articles.title: Detecting homoglyph names in Python: Cyrillic look-alikes, fullwidth letters and zero-width spaces
articles.excerpt: pаypal and paypal look identical, but the first contains a Cyrillic а (U+0430). Homoglyphs like this let someone register a name that impersonates another account, a brand or a person on a watch list,…
articles.body: pаypal and paypal look identical, but the first contains a Cyrillic а (U+0430) . Homoglyphs like this let someone register a name that impersonates another account, a brand or a person on a watch list, and they slip past exact string comparisons. Three checks catch most of them: NFKC normalisation (folds fullwidth Ｐａｙ and ligatures into plain letters), mixed-script detection (a single word that mixes Latin and Cyrillic is almost never legitimate), and a skeleton comparison that maps look-alike characters to one form before checking for collisions. Add a check for invisible characters such as the zero-width space. Here's a tested Python version, and the legitimate names it has to leave alone. Why doesn't normal comparison catch it?

articles.title: How a JSON payload is converted to a JWT string
articles.excerpt: Today I spent my time understanding JSON web tokens and how they work. But the thing I found the most interesting was how these long, encrypted strings are generated. So, I did a deep dive, and here i…
articles.body: Today I spent my time understanding JSON web tokens and how they work. But the thing I found the most interesting was how these long, encrypted strings are generated. So, I did a deep dive, and here is what I learned: Converting raw JSON into a long JWT string comes down to two main steps: encoding and signing. Step 1: Base64URL Encoding (Formatting) First, the JWT needs two separate JSON objects: Header: the metadata (e.g., {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"} ) Payload: which contains your JSON user data/claims (e.g., {"userId": 123, "role": "admin"} ). Both JSON strings are converted into bytes and encoded using Base64URL. Base64URL is a standard Base64 encoding, but modified to be URL-safe.

articles.excerpt: Open data from NASA’s Fermi mission helped an international team of scientists develop a method for finding pulsars about a million times faster than before.
articles.body: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters.

articles.body: Aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer. It’s going to Martin Hartono, the startup’s No. 1 “Accelerator” investor, and it’s being exported out of the US. It’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022. And it comes a week after Aptera reported $9.2 million in cash against the roughly $25 million it says it needs to start series production. more…

articles.title: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
articles.excerpt: Canva will now allow you to turn off its generative AI features. With this change, you can disable the graphic design platform's array of AI tools, such as its AI photo-extending Magic Expand feature,…
articles.body: Canva will now allow you to turn off its generative AI features. With this change , you can disable the graphic design platform's array of AI tools, such as its AI photo-extending Magic Expand feature, as well as turn off the ability to generate images with its Canva chatbot . This toggle doesn't turn off every AI-powered feature on Canva, however. That includes Canva's background remover and its Magic Grab tool, which lets you select an object in an image and move it somewhere else. Canva says these tools will stay on because they "make everyday tasks faster without generating anything new." The toggle still turns off many of Canva's other … Read the full story at The Verge.
